prerequisites: very good knowledge in object-oriented programming

learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully completed this module can analyze a given task with regard to a program system to be created and elaborate the requirements for it. They are able to design class diagrams using known design patterns. They understand the connections between analysis, design, and implementation.
Students who have successfully completed this module can discuss requirements and explain connections within software development using UML models.

Students who have successfully completed this module can assess the quality of requirements, possess knowledge of the essential diagrams of the Unified Modeling Language (UML) and can use them appropriately during software development.

Students who have successfully completed this module possess knowledge of the essential diagrams of the Unified Modeling Language (UML) and can use them appropriately in the creation of models from requirements created by themselves or others and their implementation in software.
Students who have successfully completed this module can apply systematic procedures for creating requirements and object-oriented models to then professionally evaluate them.

Students who have successfully completed this module are able to structure and record the requirements of software system customers, thus building the bridge between technical domain and implementation.
Students who have successfully completed this module can use established procedures for the creation, analysis, and implementation of requirements as software.

syllabus_topics: Object-oriented modeling of classes using UML diagrams
Visualization and analysis of the interaction of objects
assessment_rules: Graded assessment can be an oral examination, a written project report (minimum 12 pages with a ~6 minute pitch), or a term paper (minimum 15 pages). Ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of weekly task sheets with practice exercises. Specific duration for oral examination is as per the general examination regulations.
